This study examines the procurement of redispatch services by a grid operator within a market characterized by an all-or-none order design. We demonstrate that this design is optimal for the operator when the redispatch service is a public good, as it ensures the operator can procure the service at the lowest possible cost. Furthermore, we show that the operator can achieve the same cost efficiency by implementing a uniform pricing scheme.

This paper establishes a polynomial analogue of the Bateman-Horn conjecture for function fields over finite fields. Specifically, it demonstrates that for any finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$ and any finite set of irreducible polynomials $f_1, \dots, f_k \in \mathbb{F}_q[x]$ that share no common roots, the Galois group of the polynomial $f_1(x) \cdots f_k(x)$ over $\mathbb{F}_q$ is the full symmetric group $S_k$.

This study examines the impact of top quark pair production on the detection of Higgs boson signals in the $H \to \gamma\gamma$ decay channel. We analyze the $H \to \gamma\gamma$ signal within the context of the $t\bar{t}H$ production process, focusing on the $t\bar{t}H \to b\bar{b}W^+W^-\gamma\gamma$ final state. Our analysis utilizes the ATLAS detector data from the LHC, covering a center-of-mass energy of $\sqrt{s} = 13$ TeV and an integrated luminosity of 139 fb$^{-1}$. We observe that the $t\bar{t}H$ process significantly influences the $H \to \gamma\gamma$ signal, particularly in the high invariant mass region of the diphoton system.

We examine the Higgsstrahlung process, $e^+e^- \to ZH$, within the context of extended scalar sectors, focusing on the Higgs diphoton decay rate. We demonstrate that the Higgsstrahlung cross section is highly sensitive to the Higgs diphoton decay rate, allowing for the determination of the Higgs diphoton branching ratio with a precision of approximately 10% at a center-of-mass energy of 250 GeV.

Saturn's south pole exhibits a polar stratospheric vortex (PSV) during its summer season, a phenomenon that contrasts with the absence of such a feature at the north pole. This study utilizes Cassini Composite Infrared Spectrometer (CIRS) data to investigate the north polar stratospheric vortex (NPSV) during Saturn's northern summer. The findings reveal that the NPSV is characterized by a cold, high-pressure core, a structure that mirrors the southern counterpart. Furthermore, the NPSV displays a distinct asymmetry, with its western flank being significantly colder than its eastern side. This asymmetry is attributed to the influence of the northern Hadley circulation, which drives a poleward flow of air from the equator.

This study examines the Schrödinger equation with a potential $V$ defined on a bounded domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$, subject to Dirichlet boundary conditions. We establish that classical blow-up techniques, which typically rely on the virial identity, can be adapted to this setting. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the virial identity remains valid even when the potential $V$ is merely locally integrable.

This paper introduces a new theory of characteristic-zero commutative algebra, which is built upon the foundations of positive-characteristic algebra. The theory is designed to be compatible with the existing framework of positive-characteristic algebra.

We present a comprehensive study of the breakdown of the "sum rules of spectral weight" during the metal-insulator transition in strongly correlated systems. This phenomenon is observed in the context of the Mott transition, where the total spectral weight remains constant, yet the distribution of weight between the lower and upper Hubbard bands shifts. We demonstrate that this redistribution is driven by the emergence of a new, broad spectral feature in the lower Hubbard band, which we identify as a "mid-gap" state. This state is characterized by a finite lifetime and a broad energy distribution, and it is shown to be a direct consequence of the transition from a Mott insulator to a metal.

This study examines the quantum state of a quantum double dark-soliton, which is characterized by a density profile that evolves from a single soliton to a double soliton as the system's energy increases. We demonstrate that this state can be described by a superposition of two single solitons, where the relative phase between them is determined by the system's energy. Furthermore, we show that the energy of this state is directly proportional to the relative phase.

This paper introduces the notion of a symplectical double vector bundle, which serves as a symplectical analogue to the concept of a symmetric $k$-fold vector bundle. We demonstrate that the symplectical double vector bundle is a specific instance of a symplectical $k$-fold vector bundle. Furthermore, we establish a correspondence between the symplectical double vector bundle and the symplectical $k$-fold vector bundle, showing that the former is a particular case of the latter.

This paper introduces a geometric measure on orbits within the context of Kirillov's orbit method for Lie algebras. We demonstrate that this measure is invariant under the action of the group and coincides with Kirillov's measure when the group is unimodular. Furthermore, we establish that the measure is invariant under the action of the group.

This study introduces a novel phase retrieval algorithm designed to reconstruct energy spectra from x-ray scattering experiments. The method employs a non-iterative approach that utilizes a single measurement to recover the phase of the scattering function, thereby enabling the reconstruction of the energy spectrum. This technique is demonstrated using data from a recent experiment conducted at the Advanced Photon Source, where it successfully recovers the energy spectrum of a liquid sample.

This work explores the application of classical disordered statistical mechanics models to analyze quantum error correcting codes. Specifically, we examine the classical ground state of a disordered Ising model on a random graph, where the disorder originates from the random graph's structure. We demonstrate that the ground state of this system is equivalent to the ground state of a specific quantum error correcting code. Furthermore, we show that the ground state energy of the classical model serves as a proxy for the code's distance. Finally, we establish that the ground state energy of the classical model is directly related to the code's weight enumerator.

This study examines the electronic properties of a quantum-well structure composed of Tellurene (Te) and Tellurium (Te) layers, focusing on the effects of strain engineering. We demonstrate that applying strain to this system can induce a significant non-trivial gap, with a magnitude of approximately 0.1 eV.

This study introduces a novel method for modeling blocking fractures in fractured porous media by employing the Dirac-$\beta$ function approach. This technique allows for the representation of fractures as a continuous distribution of apertures, thereby eliminating the need to explicitly define individual fracture geometries. The proposed model is validated against a standard discrete fracture model, demonstrating that it accurately reproduces the macroscopic flow behavior of the system.

We present a theoretical investigation into the magnetic control of spin-valve behavior at moderately low exchange fields. Our analysis reveals that the spin-valve effect is governed by the interplay between the exchange field and the spin-orbit field, which is induced by the spin-orbit interaction. This interaction generates a spin-orbit field that opposes the exchange field, thereby reducing the total effective field. Consequently, the spin-valve effect is significantly enhanced when the exchange field is weak.

This paper introduces a novel framework for hypothesis selection that integrates utility functions to evaluate the value of each hypothesis. By employing a utility function, the model assesses the worth of a hypothesis based on its potential to enhance the quality of the selected decision. The proposed method is evaluated on a dataset of 1,000 instances, demonstrating that it outperforms existing approaches in both accuracy and efficiency.

Discourse markers (DMs) are essential for conveying semantic relations between sentences, yet their study remains limited by the scarcity of available datasets. To address this, we introduce DiscSense, a new dataset comprising 1,000 pairs of sentences annotated with both semantic relations and the specific DMs that connect them. We also provide a baseline model for semantic relation classification that utilizes these markers. Our experiments demonstrate that incorporating DiscSense significantly enhances the performance of state-of-the-art models on the RTE-1 task, achieving a 1.5% improvement in F1 score.

This study examines the nonradiative decay of the first excited state in the 1,1-dimethyl-2,2,2-trifluoroethane (DMTE) radical cation, which is generated via photoionization of DMTE. The analysis utilizes the Mott-Seitz model to determine the energy barrier for this process, finding it to be 0.14 eV. This value aligns with the energy barrier for the reverse reaction, the recombination of the DMTE radical cation with an electron.

This paper introduces a novel training algorithm for neural networks that eliminates the need for backpropagation. Unlike traditional methods, this approach computes errors directly at the output layer and propagates them forward to the input layer, bypassing the backward pass entirely. The proposed method is demonstrated to be effective on the MNIST dataset, achieving a test accuracy of 98.5%.

This study examines a model of magnetic skyrmions on a two-dimensional lattice, where the target space is the $n$-sphere $S^n$. We demonstrate that the homotopy group $\pi_n(S^n)$, which is isomorphic to the integers $\mathbb{Z}$, determines the possible skyrmion types. Specifically, the $k$-th homotopy class corresponds to a skyrmion carrying a topological charge of $k$. Furthermore, we show that the energy of these skyrmions increases with their topological charge.

This study examines the convergence of the Hartree-Fock method for a system of electrons interacting via Coulomb forces, where the interaction strength is scaled by a parameter $\alpha$. We demonstrate that the Hartree-Fock energy functional is convex for $\alpha \leq 1$, ensuring the existence of a global minimum. Furthermore, we establish that the Hartree-Fock energy converges to the true ground state energy as $\alpha \to 0$.

This study examines the interplay between dynamical and structural disorder in the context of explosive synchronization transitions. We demonstrate that the presence of structural disorder can significantly alter the nature of the transition, shifting it from a continuous to a discontinuous type. Furthermore, we show that the degree of discontinuity is governed by the ratio of dynamical to structural disorder.

This study examines the geodesic properties of factorized objectives within matrix optimization, specifically focusing on the restricted strong convexity and smoothness of the underlying objective function. We demonstrate that if the objective function satisfies these conditions, the factorized objective inherits them, albeit with modified constants. Furthermore, we establish that the factorized objective is geodesically strongly convex and smooth on the Stiefel manifold whenever the original objective function is geodesically strongly convex and smooth on the same manifold.

In 1990, Borodin, Kostochka, and Woodall conjectured that every bipartite graph with a maximum degree of 3 requires at most 5 colors for a strong edge-coloring. This paper confirms the conjecture for the specific case of cubic bipartite graphs.
This paper examines the identities of Dirichlet $L$-functions, specifically focusing on the Gauss sums associated with the characters involved.

We examine the impact of heavy particles on the stochastic gravitational-wave background (SGWB) generated by first-order phase transitions (FOPTs) in the early universe. We demonstrate that the presence of heavy particles can significantly alter the SGWB spectrum, potentially leading to a misinterpretation of the phase transition's nature if these effects are overlooked. Furthermore, we show that the inclusion of heavy particles can resolve the tension between the observed Hubble tension and the constraints derived from the SGWB.

This study examines the locomotion of helical swimmers in a fluid environment, focusing on the "snowman-like effect" that arises from the interaction between the swimmer's helical shape and the surrounding fluid. We demonstrate that this effect is driven by the swimmer's helical geometry and the resulting fluid flow patterns. Furthermore, we show that the snowman-like effect can be utilized to enhance the swimming speed of helical swimmers.

This study examines the expected Hamming distance from Nash Equilibrium in co-evolutionary genetic algorithms (CEGAs) under both social and individual learning frameworks. We demonstrate that the expected distance in the social learning scenario is significantly greater than that in the individual learning scenario. Furthermore, we establish that the expected distance in the social learning case is bounded by a constant, whereas the expected distance in the individual learning case is bounded by a constant.

This study introduces a novel approach for extracting security-related concepts from text by leveraging Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) networks. The method utilizes a dataset comprising 1,000 sentences sourced from the MITRE ATT&CK framework, which details adversary tactics, techniques, and procedures. The proposed model was evaluated against a baseline using the F1 score, demonstrating a 10% improvement in performance.

This study examines a mixed opinion formation model where agents adopt either a binary stance or a neutral position, with the latter being influenced by the average magnetization of the binary group. We demonstrate that the average magnetization of the binary group in this mixed model is identical to that of a pure Ising model, provided the binary group's magnetization is treated as an external field. Furthermore, we show that the average magnetization of the neutral group in the mixed model corresponds to the average magnetization of a pure Ising model under an external field equal to the binary group's magnetization.

The transmission of COVID-19 is primarily driven by the spread of respiratory droplets, which are influenced by factors such as droplet size, environmental conditions, and the distance between individuals. This study employs a stochastic model to examine the transmission dynamics of COVID-19, specifically analyzing the impact of droplet size and environmental conditions on infection rates. The model incorporates a stochastic differential equation (SDE) framework to account for the inherent randomness in the transmission process. By utilizing the stochastic Lyapunov function method, we establish the existence and uniqueness of a global positive solution for the proposed SDE system. Furthermore, we derive the conditions under which the disease will either die out or become endemic. Finally, numerical simulations are conducted to validate the theoretical findings.

Neural networks have recently emerged as a powerful tool for solving inverse and ill-posed problems, offering advantages over traditional methods by requiring minimal prior knowledge and demonstrating robustness to noise. This paper introduces a new framework for solving inverse problems that leverages the inherent inductive biases of neural networks. We propose a novel approach that combines a neural network with a variational formulation of the problem, where the network is trained to minimize the discrepancy between the model's output and the observed data. This method is designed to be flexible, allowing for the integration of various neural architectures and the incorporation of different types of prior information. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this framework through several numerical experiments, including image deblurring, image inpainting, and image super-resolution.

This study examines the relationship between the ordinary and symbolic powers of edge ideals within weighted oriented graphs. It establishes that these powers coincide if and only if the graph is a forest. Furthermore, the paper provides a characterization of the equality between the ordinary and symbolic powers of edge ideals for weighted oriented graphs that are not forests.

This study introduces a novel non-uniform range restriction method designed to prevent silent data corruptions in neural networks. Unlike existing techniques that apply uniform bounds to all weights, our approach allows for varying limits across different parameters. We demonstrate that this flexibility enables the method to achieve a significantly higher level of robustness against adversarial attacks compared to uniform strategies. Furthermore, we provide a theoretical analysis showing that the proposed method can attain the same robustness as uniform range restriction while utilizing a much smaller total range.

Netting, the process of offsetting mutual obligations between parties, is a critical component of modern financial systems. This study introduces a novel graph-based algorithm designed to identify the optimal netting solution for an economy, thereby minimizing the total number of transactions required. The proposed method is evaluated against a standard greedy algorithm using a dataset of 100,000 transactions, demonstrating that the new approach achieves a 10% reduction in transaction volume.

This study introduces a generalized Jordanian twist, which extends the simple Jordanian twist by incorporating a non-trivial $R$-matrix. We demonstrate that this generalized twist is equivalent to the simple Jordanian twist when the $R$-matrix is trivial. Furthermore, we establish that the generalized twist is a solution to the quantum Yang-Baxter equation.

This study introduces a novel method for identifying named entities in low-resource languages, specifically focusing on the task of recognizing language names. The approach leverages a pre-trained language model to generate contextualized embeddings for each token, which are then fed into a BiLSTM-CRF architecture to predict entity boundaries. The model is trained using a combination of character-level and word-level features. Evaluated on the CoNLL-2012 dataset, this method achieves a 1.5% increase in F1 score compared to the previous state-of-the-art results.

This study examines the evolution of particle ratios across a spectrum of collision systems, ranging from small to large scales, within high-energy collisions. The analysis reveals that the ratios of protons to pions, protons to kaons, and protons to anti-protons exhibit a consistent trend: they increase as the system size grows. This behavior is observed across various collision types, including proton-proton, proton-lead, and lead-lead interactions.

Dialogue state tracking (DST) is a vital component of task-oriented dialogue systems, yet it is frequently hindered by the scarcity of annotated data. To address this, researchers have increasingly turned to semi-supervised learning (SSL) to leverage unlabeled data. However, the effectiveness of SSL is often compromised by noisy labels in the training set, which can lead to poor model performance. This paper introduces a novel approach that combines SSL with label noise correction to enhance DST. Specifically, we propose a method that utilizes a pre-trained language model to generate pseudo-labels for unlabeled data, which are then used to train a noise-robust model. Our experiments on the MultiWOZ dataset demonstrate that this approach significantly outperforms existing methods, achieving a 1.5% improvement in joint goal accuracy and a 1.2% increase in slot F1 score.

This study examines the role of urban infrastructure in shaping civil unrest dynamics, utilizing a model where agents occupy nodes within a city's road network. Agents are classified as either peaceful or violent, with the latter capable of converting peaceful individuals through direct contact. The research demonstrates that the network's topology significantly impacts the system's behavior, revealing that cities with higher average degrees and lower clustering coefficients are more susceptible to widespread unrest. Furthermore, the findings indicate that the spatial distribution of violence is not uniform; instead, it tends to concentrate in specific areas, a pattern that is notably influenced by the underlying network structure.

We utilize the Prospector Bayesian inference framework to analyze the spectral energy distributions (SEDs) of 1,000 galaxies from the COSMOS2015 catalog, employing a suite of 1,000 mock SEDs generated with the EAZY code to evaluate the framework's performance. Our analysis reveals that Prospector accurately recovers the true star formation rates (SFRs) and stellar masses of these galaxies, with the accuracy of SFR estimates improving as the true SFR increases. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the framework's ability to recover the true SFRs is significantly enhanced by incorporating Br$ eta$ luminosity measurements.

We establish that this maximum number is determined by the rank of the matrices within the Gram spectrahedron. The FASERν experiment, located at the LHC, is designed to detect neutrinos produced by proton-proton collisions. This study presents the first results from FASERν, which are based on an analysis of 139 fb$^{-1}$ of data collected at a center-of-mass energy of 13 TeV. The analysis focuses on the charged-current quasi-elastic (CCQE) scattering of neutrinos on electrons and protons, utilizing a Monte Carlo simulation to model the expected event rates. The findings are consistent with the Standard Model predictions, allowing for the establishment of new constraints on leptonic non-unitarity. These new limits are significantly more stringent than those derived from existing CKM non-unitarity constraints.

This paper introduces a symbolic decision procedure for verifying containment between regular expressions, utilizing Brzozowski's operator to symbolically represent the left quotient of a regular expression with a string. The approach is demonstrated to be effective for practical applications, as evidenced by its implementation in the tool RE2C.

Visual-inertial odometry (VIO) is a critical technology for autonomous navigation, yet it remains vulnerable to failures caused by environmental changes and sensor noise. While traditional VIO algorithms rely on hand-crafted features, deep learning-based VIO models have emerged as a promising alternative by utilizing end-to-end learning to extract features directly from raw sensor data. However, these models often struggle with generalization when encountering new environments. This paper introduces a novel deep learning-based VIO framework that incorporates a new data augmentation strategy to improve robustness. The proposed method employs a two-stage approach: first, it trains a deep learning model on a large-scale dataset of diverse environments to learn robust feature representations; second, it fine-tunes this model on a smaller dataset specific to the target environment. Experimental results demonstrate that this approach significantly outperforms existing methods in both accuracy and robustness.

This study introduces a new class of three-dimensional topological semimetals, termed "square-root topological semimetals," which exhibit a higher-order Weyl semimetal structure. These systems are characterized by a unique square-root topology, where the Berry curvature is concentrated on a two-dimensional surface rather than at isolated points. This phenomenon arises from the square-root nature of the energy dispersion relation near the surface. The research demonstrates that this square-root topology can be realized in a three-dimensional Dirac semimetal by introducing a specific type of surface potential.

This study introduces a numerical method for solving data completion problems using edge finite elements. The approach relies on a variational formulation of the problem, which is then discretized using edge finite elements. The resulting discrete system is solved via a preconditioned conjugate gradient algorithm. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the method is effective and efficient.

This study examines the parafermion vertex operator algebra (VOA) associated with the simple affine Lie superalgebra $osp(1|2n)$, specifically focusing on the case where the level is $k=1$. We demonstrate that this parafermion VOA is isomorphic to the simple affine VOA of type $A_{2n-1}$ at level $k=1$. Furthermore, we establish that the generators of the parafermion VOA correspond to the generators of the affine VOA of type $A_{2n-1}$ at level $k=1$.

This study introduces a novel method for knowledge amalgamation that leverages saliency maps to identify and transfer the most significant features from a teacher model to a student model. By utilizing saliency maps to pinpoint the most relevant features, the proposed approach ensures that the student model learns the most critical information from the teacher. The effectiveness of this method is demonstrated through experiments on the CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 datasets, where it outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques.

Grid cells, located in the entorhinal cortex, are essential for spatial navigation and memory, functioning as a neural compass that encodes an animal's position within its environment. While these cells are known to be sensitive to external cues, the specific mechanisms by which they integrate such information remain unclear. This study investigates how grid cells respond to external cues by examining the impact of cue rotation on grid cell firing patterns in rats. The findings indicate that grid cells are highly sensitive to the orientation of external cues, with the degree of sensitivity varying based on the specific cue type. Furthermore, the research demonstrates that grid cells can adapt to changes in cue orientation, suggesting a dynamic process of recalibration. These results provide new insights into the mechanisms underlying grid cell function and their role in spatial navigation.

This study examines the impact of kinematic dynamos on magnetic cycles in slowly rotating stars, utilizing a model that incorporates a mean-field dynamo with a turbulent magnetic diffusivity that varies with depth. The analysis reveals that the dynamo's efficiency is highly sensitive to the depth of the tachocline, the region separating the radiative and convective zones. Specifically, a deeper tachocline correlates with a higher likelihood of magnetic cycles. Furthermore, the research indicates that the presence of a tachocline is a necessary condition for the emergence of magnetic cycles in these systems.
This paper addresses the question of how many S4 quartic extensions exist such that certain elliptic curves do not gain rank, according to conditions specified for their rational rank.

We examine the production of irreversible entropy during quantum quenches in a one-dimensional spin-1/2 Heisenberg antiferromagnetic chain. Our analysis reveals that the irreversible entropy production is directly proportional to the change in entropy and inversely proportional to the change in temperature. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the irreversible entropy production is a universal quantity, remaining independent of the specific initial state and the nature of the quench.

This study examines the time-twirling of the initial system-plus-environment state within non-unitary dynamics, demonstrating that the resulting distinguishability time is inversely proportional to the rate of decoherence. Furthermore, we establish that the time-twirling of the initial state is equivalent to the time-twirling of the initial system state, provided the environment is initially in a pure state.

This paper addresses the problem of determining the maximum number of interpolation nodes that can be placed within the unit cube $Q_n$ such that a nondegenerate regular simplex exists in $\mathbb{R}^n$ with these nodes as its vertices. We establish that such a simplex exists if and only if the number of nodes $N$ satisfies the condition $N \leq n+1$. Furthermore, we provide a constructive proof demonstrating that for any $N$ meeting this bound, a nondegenerate regular simplex can indeed be formed.

This study examines the electrical characteristics of etched silicon, specifically focusing on the impact of etching on carrier concentration and mobility. The findings indicate that etched silicon exhibits a significantly higher carrier concentration compared to buffer oxide etched silicon, with a corresponding reduction in mobility.

This paper establishes cdh descent and Milnor excision for twisted homotopy K-theory, utilizing these results to prove that the cdh descent property holds for the twisted K-theory of the classifying space of a finite group.

This study examines the long-term evolution of a planet's atmosphere through the lens of interior-exterior cycling, utilizing a coupled model that integrates a 1D radiative-convective atmosphere with a 1D interior structure. We apply this framework to a super-Earth with a mass of 5.5 Earth masses and a radius of 1.5 Earth radii, which possesses a hydrogen-helium envelope and a rocky core. Our results indicate that the planet's atmospheric mass is highly sensitive to the initial core mass fraction, with a 10% increase in this fraction leading to a 10% reduction in atmospheric mass. Furthermore, we find that the planet's atmospheric mass is also significantly influenced by the initial atmospheric mass fraction, where a 10% increase in the initial atmospheric mass results in a 10% increase in the final atmospheric mass. Finally, we demonstrate that the planet's atmospheric mass is also significantly influenced by the initial atmospheric mass fraction, where a 10% increase in the initial atmospheric mass results in a 10% increase in the final atmospheric mass.

This study examines the dissociative electron attachment (DEA) of 1,2-propanediol (1,2-PDO) and 1,3-propanediol (1,3-PDO) using electron energies ranging from 0 to 20 eV. The findings reveal that DEA in 1,2-PDO is primarily driven by the formation of methyl cations, whereas DEA in 1,3-PDO is dominated by the formation of ethyl cations. These results indicate that the structural arrangement of the hydroxyl groups significantly influences the DEA mechanism.

Tensor networks are a powerful tool for representing and simulating quantum states, yet their application to quantum computing is often hindered by the difficulty of mapping them to parametrized quantum circuits. This paper introduces a method to convert tensor networks into quantum circuits by utilizing a specific class of tensor networks known as projected entangled pair states (PEPS). The proposed approach is demonstrated on a two-dimensional lattice of qubits, where the resulting circuit is shown to be capable of generating the ground state of a two-dimensional Heisenberg model.

This study introduces a novel graph neural network (GNN) framework designed to classify tissue representations derived from whole-slide images (WSIs) in cancer research. The proposed method constructs a graph where nodes represent image patches and edges are determined by the spatial proximity of these patches. By integrating both the visual features of the patches and their spatial relationships, the model effectively captures the contextual information inherent in the tissue architecture. Experimental evaluations on three distinct datasets demonstrate that this approach achieves state-of-the-art performance in classifying cancer types.

This study introduces a nonlinear Hawkes process designed to model multivariate point processes, where the intensity of each process is determined by a nonlinear function of the past event history. We establish the existence and uniqueness of the process's solution and demonstrate that it converges to a stationary distribution. Furthermore, we derive the stationary distribution's explicit form and provide a method for estimating the model's parameters.

This study introduces a novel, highly efficient implementation of the Fast Multipole Method (FMM) designed for astrophysical simulations. The approach is built upon a hierarchical octree structure, which is populated using a fast, parallelized algorithm. The FMM itself is executed in parallel, with the computational domain divided into subdomains to facilitate this. The method is validated through a series of tests, including a comparison with a standard $O(N^2)$ algorithm, a benchmark against a highly optimized $O(N \log N)$ implementation, and a demonstration of its performance on a large-scale simulation of a galaxy cluster.

This study introduces Contrastive Semi-supervised learning for Cross Anatomy Domain Adaptation (CS-CADA), a novel framework designed to enhance segmentation performance across different anatomical domains. CS-CADA leverages a contrastive learning strategy to align the feature representations of unlabeled source images with those of labeled target images, thereby facilitating effective domain adaptation. Furthermore, the method incorporates a semi-supervised learning component that utilizes pseudo-labels generated from unlabeled target data to further refine the model. Experimental evaluations conducted on the MICCAI 2018 Cross-Modality Domain Adaptation Challenge demonstrate that CS-CADA achieves state-of-the-art results, surpassing existing methods in both segmentation accuracy and robustness.

This study demonstrates that a proper understanding of 3+1 dimensional supergravity requires a correct grasp of BRS symmetry. We present a new, self-contained derivation of the BRS symmetry for 3+1 dimensional supergravity, which is based on the supergravity action and the supergravity field equations.

This study examines the generation of circularly polarized light through the interaction of a linearly polarized laser pulse with a plasma waveplate. The waveplate is created by a transverse magnetic field that induces a circularly polarized plasma wave, which in turn rotates the polarization of the incident laser. The required thickness of this waveplate is determined by the plasma electron density and the magnetic field strength. The research demonstrates that the waveplate's thickness can be adjusted by varying the magnetic field, allowing for the control of the laser's polarization state.

This study examines the type-II two-Higgs doublet extension of the Standard Model, which incorporates a CP-violating phase within the Higgs sector. We demonstrate that this framework can generate a tau electric dipole moment (EDM) exceeding the current experimental limits, provided the CP-violating phase is sufficiently large.

This paper examines the error correction capabilities of rank metric codes, specifically focusing on the distinction between rates below and above 1/2. For codes with rates less than 1/2, we establish that the error correction capability is determined by the minimum distance of the code. Conversely, for codes with rates exceeding 1/2, we demonstrate that the error correction capability is governed by the minimum distance of the dual code.

This study examines the operator product expansion (OPE) blocks of conserved currents within two-dimensional conformal field theories (CFT$_{2}$) and their holographic counterparts in three-dimensional anti-de Sitter space (AdS$_{3}$). We demonstrate that, unlike the case in AdS$_{3}$, these OPE blocks in AdS$_{2}$ cannot be represented as a sum of geodesic operators. Instead, they are expressed as a linear combination of geodesic operators and a specific non-geodesic operator. This non-geodesic component is identified as the OPE block of a scalar field in AdS$_{2}$, which is dual to a primary operator in CFT$_{2}$ with a conformal dimension $\Delta = 1$.

This study introduces a novel neural network approach for reconstructing gravitational lensing, which is designed to surpass the performance of traditional estimators. The proposed method utilizes a convolutional neural network (CNN) to learn the mapping between the observed image and the underlying mass distribution. We demonstrate that this technique achieves superior results compared to standard estimators, such as the maximum likelihood estimator (MLE) and the maximum a posteriori (MAP) estimator, across various scenarios. Furthermore, the CNN-based method exhibits greater robustness against noise and maintains high accuracy even when the mass distribution is non-Gaussian.

In 1973, Gelfand and MacPherson introduced a combinatorial differential manifold, now known as the Gelfand-MacPherson manifold, which is associated with a specific arrangement of hyperplanes. This paper explores the relationship between the Gelfand-MacPherson manifold and the combinatorial differential manifold defined by a hyperplane arrangement.

We present the discovery of SN~2020jfo, a Type Ia supernova located in the galaxy NGC~4490 at a distance of 19.8 Mpc. This event was identified through the Zwicky Transient Facility (ZTF) and confirmed by the Las Cumbres Observatory Global Telescope Network (LCOGT). Our analysis of the light curve and spectral data indicates that SN~2020jfo is a normal Type Ia supernova, with a peak absolute magnitude of $M_B = -19.35 \pm 0.10$ and a stretch parameter of $s = 0.96 \pm 0.03$. Spectral features observed at maximum light, including the Si II $\lambda$6355 line, are consistent with those of standard Type Ia events. Furthermore, our modeling of the ejecta suggests a Ni/Fe production ratio of 0.07, which aligns with the solar value.

This study introduces a novel method for determining the azimuthal rotation angle of a cross-like image, which is essential for identifying the specific segments of a lobster-eye optics system. The approach relies on analyzing the image's azimuthal rotation angle, which is derived from the cross-like image's orientation. The method's effectiveness is demonstrated through simulations and experimental data, showing that it can accurately determine the rotation angle with a precision of approximately 0.01 degrees.

This paper introduces a novel level set approach for analyzing second-order fully nonlinear equations, specifically targeting the Dirichlet problem for the infinity Laplacian. The method employs a level set formulation to define the solution as the envelope of a family of solutions to a linearized equation. This framework facilitates the derivation of a priori estimates and the proof of existence and uniqueness for the Dirichlet problem. Furthermore, the approach is extended to establish the existence and uniqueness of solutions for the Dirichlet problem involving the infinity Laplacian with a source term.

We examine the impact of a density-only model on halo mass prediction accuracy within cosmological simulations featuring an initial scalar perturbation amplitude of $\sigma_8 = 0.8$. Our findings indicate that this model yields a 10% improvement in accuracy compared to the standard $\Lambda$CDM framework.

This study introduces a novel semi-supervised approach for piano transcription that integrates low-rank matrix factorization with deep learning. The method employs a two-stage process: first, a supervised deep learning model is trained to generate initial estimates of the piano score, which are then used to initialize a semi-supervised CNMF algorithm. This algorithm leverages the initial estimates alongside a small set of labeled data to refine the transcription. Experimental results demonstrate that this semi-supervised CNMF method outperforms both state-of-the-art low-rank factorization techniques and supervised deep learning approaches.

This study introduces a novel method for assigning properties such as mass and specific angular momentum to fluid elements within rotating stars, utilizing a Lagrangian framework. This approach is designed to be applicable to any stellar model, regardless of the specific equation of state or the presence of magnetic fields. The method is demonstrated using a rotating, non-magnetic, polytropic model, where the results are compared against those obtained from the traditional Eulerian approach. The findings indicate that the Lagrangian method yields a more accurate representation of the star's internal structure, particularly regarding the distribution of angular momentum.

This paper introduces a novel method for acquiring labeled data that leverages the inherent structure of the dataset. The proposed approach, termed Selective Labeling, functions by identifying and labeling only a subset of data points that are most informative for the model. This strategy is designed to enhance the efficiency of the labeling process, thereby reducing the overall cost associated with data annotation.

The detection of both gravitational and electromagnetic radiation from a neutron star merger provides a unique opportunity to study the physics of these events. This paper examines the electromagnetic signatures of a neutron star coalescence, focusing on the interaction between the neutron star and the surrounding accretion disk. We utilize a numerical model to simulate the electromagnetic emission generated by the interaction between the neutron star and the accretion disk. Our results indicate that the electromagnetic emission is dominated by the interaction between the neutron star and the accretion disk, and that the emission is strongly dependent on the mass of the neutron star. Social determinants of health (SDOH) are critical factors influencing health outcomes, yet their assessment is often hindered by the lack of standardized data collection methods. This study introduces a novel approach to extract SDOH information from clinical notes using a machine learning model trained on a dataset of 1,000 records. The model achieved an F1 score of 0.75, demonstrating its ability to identify relevant SDOH data. Furthermore, the research highlights the potential for leveraging natural language processing to uncover SDOH insights from unstructured clinical text, thereby enhancing the understanding of these vital health determinants.

This study examines the cost of transporting a swimmer between two fixed locations in a fluid environment, where the swimmer's motion is governed by a stochastic differential equation driven by a switching process. We demonstrate that the cost function is convex with respect to the switching frequency, and we derive the optimal switching frequency that minimizes this cost.

The pandemic has fundamentally altered the nature of urban encounters, with the long-term consequences for community resilience and diversity still uncertain. This study examines the impact of the pandemic on the diversity of urban interactions in the city of Barcelona, Spain, utilizing a dataset of 1.5 million geotagged tweets collected from 2019 to 2021. The analysis reveals that the pandemic significantly reduced the diversity of urban encounters, a trend that persisted even after the initial lockdowns ended. Furthermore, the research indicates that the pandemic's effects were not uniform across the city; instead, they varied by neighborhood, with the most pronounced declines in diversity occurring in areas that were already less diverse prior to the crisis.

We investigate the impact of migrating objects on the inner regions of circumstellar discs around high-mass young stellar objects (YSOs). Our findings indicate that the presence of a single migrating object can destabilize the inner disc, leading to the formation of a gap. This gap subsequently causes the disc to become unstable, resulting in the inward migration of the object. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the disc's stability is highly sensitive to the mass of the migrating object, with the critical mass required to induce instability decreasing as the disc's viscosity increases.

This paper introduces a scattering theory for a class of non-compact quantum systems, specifically those with a non-compact configuration space. The theory is defined by an asymptotic algebra and a scattering matrix, which together characterize the system's dynamics. We demonstrate that the scattering matrix is uniquely determined by the asymptotic algebra and the system's Hamiltonian. Furthermore, we establish that the asymptotic algebra is uniquely determined by the scattering matrix and the Hamiltonian. Finally, we prove that the scattering matrix is uniquely determined by the asymptotic algebra and the Hamiltonian.

This study examines the exposure levels from 5G cellular towers, specifically analyzing how building attenuation affects these levels. The research compares 5G exposure against pre-5G technology, highlighting that 5G signals are more susceptible to attenuation by buildings. Consequently, the study concludes that 5G exposure is significantly lower than that of pre-5G systems.

This study introduces a novel method for reconstructing the surface elevation of water waves from their envelope, utilizing a nonlinear wave equation that incorporates a specific nonlinear term. This approach is applicable to a wide range of wave scenarios, including those with varying depths and those influenced by currents. The method is demonstrated through a numerical example involving a solitary wave, which is reconstructed from its envelope using the proposed technique.
This paper presents a proof of the surface layer theorem for differential forms defined on locally convex spaces.

This study introduces a layered control system designed for mobile platforms equipped with sonar sensors, enabling them to navigate autonomously in unknown environments. The architecture consists of two primary layers: a high-level layer that generates a global path using a probabilistic roadmap (PRM) algorithm, and a low-level layer that executes local obstacle avoidance and path following. The system was evaluated in a simulated environment, demonstrating its ability to successfully navigate a maze-like structure.

This study introduces a novel approach to fake news detection that leverages contextual information from social media platforms. By utilizing the contextual data surrounding news articles, the proposed method aims to enhance detection accuracy. The research evaluates this approach using the FakeNewsNet dataset, demonstrating that incorporating contextual information significantly improves performance compared to models relying solely on textual content.

This study examines the impact of curvature on the phase transition of a two-dimensional Ising model with a square lattice, where the system is confined within a circular boundary. We find that the curvature effect is directly linked to the system's entropy change, which in turn drives the emergence of hysteresis.

This study introduces a suboptimal decoding order selection policy for the successive interference cancellation (SIC) receiver in a multiuser multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) system. The proposed method is designed to reduce computational complexity while maintaining performance comparable to the optimal approach. Theoretical analysis demonstrates that the suboptimal policy achieves the same diversity order as the optimal policy. Furthermore, the paper provides a closed-form expression for the outage probability of the suboptimal policy, which is validated through numerical simulations.

This study introduces a novel alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) approach for the two-block reformulation of rotationally invariant L1-PCA. The proposed algorithm is proven to converge to a stationary point of the original problem. Furthermore, we establish that the method converges to a global optimum when the data matrix is rank-1.

Semantic labeling is a critical task in computer vision, yet the quality of its annotations often remains unverified. This paper introduces a novel method to validate label consistency by leveraging paraphrase tasks. The approach involves generating paraphrases for each label and then training a model to predict the original label from these paraphrases. The model's performance on this paraphrase task serves as a proxy for assessing the quality of the original annotations. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this method on the Cityscapes dataset, showing that it successfully identifies and corrects labeling errors.

This paper investigates the union of prefix-independent half-positional winning conditions, demonstrating that such a union can yield a condition that is not half-positional. Furthermore, we establish that the union of prefix-independent half-positional conditions is itself prefix-independent.

We present the results of a study on the X-ray spectra of 11 asynchronous polars, utilizing data from the XMM-Newton and Chandra observatories. Our analysis reveals that the X-ray spectra of asynchronous polars are generally similar to those of standard polars, with the notable exception of the system V471 Tau, which exhibits a significantly harder spectrum. Furthermore, we find that the X-ray luminosity of asynchronous polars is comparable to that of standard polars, with a mean value of approximately $10^{30}$ ergs/s.

This study examines a partitioned strategy for solving fluid-structure interaction (FSI) problems, where the fluid and solid components are solved independently using their respective solvers. The fluid domain is modeled using the Navier-Stokes equations, while the solid domain employs the linear elasticity equations. The two sub-problems are coupled through a Robin-type interface condition. The analysis demonstrates that the proposed method is unconditionally stable and converges at a rate of $O(\Delta t)$, provided the time step $\Delta t$ is sufficiently small.

This study introduces HiTMap, a novel representation for global metric maps that utilizes a hierarchical tree structure to manage navigation. Unlike traditional global maps, HiTMap allows for the creation of multiple local maps, each covering a specific area, which are then organized into a hierarchical framework. This design enables the system to handle large-scale environments by allowing the addition of new local maps as needed, while also supporting the removal of outdated ones. Furthermore, HiTMap facilitates the merging of local maps into a single global map, thereby enhancing the system's scalability and adaptability.

This study introduces a novel system designed to detect abusive content in tweets, utilizing a hybrid approach that combines a pre-trained language model with a custom classifier. The system was evaluated on the Abusive Language Identification Challenge (ALIC) 2019 dataset, achieving a macro F1 score of 0.81.

We present a new method for detecting local magnetic fields using atomic interferometry, achieving a sensitivity of 100 nT/√Hz. This technique relies on measuring the differential phase shift between two atomic wave packets that are spatially separated by 100 micrometers. The experiment was conducted in a vacuum chamber with a 100 mm diameter, where the magnetic field was generated by a current-carrying wire positioned 100 mm away from the atoms.

We demonstrate that the magnetocaloric effect can be tuned to generate distinct thermal responses for spin-up and spin-down electrons in a heterostructure composed of a ferromagnet and a superconductor. This phenomenon arises from the interplay between the superconducting proximity effect and the Zeeman effect, which together induce a spin-dependent shift in the superconducting energy gap.

This study introduces a new method for predicting light propagation through disordered media by employing an effective gap width approach. This technique is designed to overcome the limitations of local models, which often fail to account for the influence of neighboring gaps. By incorporating the effects of adjacent gaps, the model achieves a significant improvement in accuracy, particularly in scenarios involving large gap widths.

The calculus of constructions, introduced by Thierry Coquand and Gérard Huet in 1988, has profoundly influenced modern programming languages and type theory. This paper offers a comprehensive overview of the calculus of constructions, covering its foundational concepts, the associated type-checking algorithm, and its implementation within the Coq proof assistant.

This paper examines the application of entanglement concepts in quantum electronics, specifically focusing on the correlator method and the von-Neumann density-matrix method. It demonstrates that the correlator method is a more effective approach for analyzing entanglement in quantum electronic systems.

This study examines the impact of applying a Dirichlet process prior to densities in a mixture model, specifically regarding the recovery of identifiable admixture weights. We demonstrate that this prior can lead to the failure of identifiability, even when the underlying mixture components are themselves identifiable.

This study examines the two-loop anomalous dimensions of twist-four operators within the context of the AdS/CFT correspondence. We demonstrate that the two-loop corrections to the anomalous dimensions of these operators are entirely determined by the two-loop anomalous dimensions of twist-two operators. Furthermore, we establish that the two-loop anomalous dimensions of twist-two operators are fully fixed by the two-loop anomalous dimensions of twist-two operators in the planar limit.

DynaSOAr is a novel GPU memory allocator designed to enhance performance and memory efficiency for deep learning workloads. It achieves this by integrating a dynamic memory management strategy with a custom memory pool, enabling the system to adapt to varying memory demands and reduce fragmentation. Furthermore, DynaSOAr incorporates a dynamic memory migration mechanism that allows for the reallocation of memory across different GPU devices, thereby optimizing resource utilization. Evaluation results indicate that DynaSOAr outperforms existing GPU memory allocators in both performance and memory efficiency.

This study investigates the boundedness of the maximal operator and the Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator on generalized mixed Morrey spaces. Furthermore, it establishes the boundedness of the Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator on generalized mixed Morrey spaces.

This study examines the influence of spin-orbit coupling on the spatial distribution of Yu-Shiba-Rusinov (YSR) state peaks, specifically in systems featuring magnetic adatoms or dimers. We demonstrate that the spin-orbit interaction induces a shift in the YSR peak positions, a phenomenon that is particularly pronounced when the magnetic adatoms are situated on top of a superconducting substrate.

FourierMask is a novel method for generating high-resolution segmentation masks that leverages implicit functions and Fourier transforms. It operates by learning a continuous function that maps image coordinates to a scalar value, where the zero level set of this function delineates the object boundary. To achieve this, the model employs a Fourier-based representation of the implicit function, which is optimized using a differentiable rendering process. This approach allows FourierMask to produce segmentation masks with significantly higher resolution than those typically generated by standard deep learning models.
This paper establishes that the existence of complete, bounded minimal disks in $\mathbb{R}^3$ is equivalent to the spectrum of the Laplacian on a specific class of submanifolds.

This study introduces a novel method for analyzing cloud structures in satellite imagery, specifically designed to address the challenge of "veiled cores"—clouds obscured by other cloud layers. The approach employs a two-stage process: first, it identifies the core of a cloud system, and second, it determines the cloud's outer boundary. The core detection utilizes a modified watershed algorithm, while the boundary is defined by a new metric called the "cloudiness gradient," which measures the rate of change in cloudiness. This gradient is calculated using a convolutional neural network (CNN) trained on a dataset of 10,000 images. The proposed method was evaluated against a baseline that relies solely on the cloudiness gradient, demonstrating superior performance in both core and boundary detection.

This study examines the acceleration of ions within a very thin, low-density secondary layer when subjected to a negatively chirped laser pulse. The findings indicate that the secondary layer's presence significantly enhances ion acceleration, with the degree of enhancement depending on the layer's thickness and density. Furthermore, the results demonstrate that the secondary layer can effectively mitigate the detrimental effects of laser pulse chirping on ion acceleration.

We report the discovery of three transiting mini-Neptunes orbiting the nearby M dwarf star GJ 1132, with radii ranging from 1.7 to 2.1 Earth radii and orbital periods between 1.5 and 2.0 days. These planets are located within the star's habitable zone, which is defined as the region where a rocky body could maintain liquid water on its surface. Our findings indicate that the system's planets are likely tidally locked, meaning one side always faces the star. Furthermore, the innermost planet, GJ 1132b, is situated so close to its host star that it is expected to be tidally stripped of its atmosphere.

This study examines the electronic and magnetic properties of carbon and nitrogen impurities within TiO${_2}$, focusing on both substitutional and interstitial configurations. Our findings indicate that interstitial C and N atoms exhibit distinct behaviors compared to their substitutional counterparts, with interstitial C and N atoms showing a preference for the TiO${_2}$ (100) surface. Furthermore, we observe that interstitial C and N atoms are more stable than their substitutional equivalents.

This study examines the branching ratio limits for flavor-changing neutral current (FCNC) top quark decays, specifically $t \to Hq$ and $t \to Zq$, utilizing semi-elastic processes. The analysis leverages the full dataset from the ATLAS detector at the LHC, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 139 fb$^{-1}$ collected at a center-of-mass energy of 13 TeV. The results indicate that the branching ratio for $t \to Hq$ is constrained to be less than 0.0011 at 95% confidence level, while the limit for $t \to Zq$ is established at 0.0012 at the same confidence level.

The X-ray Integral Field Unit (X-IFU) on the upcoming Athena mission will enable detailed studies of turbulence within the intra-cluster medium (ICM) by measuring the line-of-sight velocity dispersion of highly ionized species, such as Fe XXV, across a wide range of temperatures. This research utilizes a suite of hydrodynamic simulations to investigate how turbulence affects the X-IFU's ability to detect these velocity dispersions. The simulations cover a broad spectrum of turbulence models, including those with varying injection scales, energy dissipation rates, and magnetic field strengths. The findings indicate that X-IFU can successfully measure velocity dispersions in the range of 100–300 km/s, which corresponds to turbulent energy dissipation rates of approximately 10^41–10^42 erg s^-1 Mpc^-3. Furthermore, the study demonstrates that X-IFU can distinguish between different turbulence models, particularly those differing in injection scale and dissipation rate, though it struggles to differentiate between models with varying magnetic field strengths.

This paper addresses the problem of determining the minimum number of colors required to edge-color a graph $G$ such that every copy of a specific subgraph $F$ contains at least one monochromatic edge. We establish a lower bound for this parameter when $F$ is a triangle, specifically proving that for any graph $G$ with $n$ vertices, the required number of colors is at least $\frac{1}{2}n^{1/3}$. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this bound is tight for the case where $G$ is a complete graph.

Our study covers a 1.5-degree field centered on Sgr A*, with a resolution of 0.02 degrees and a sensitivity of 0.02 mJy per beam. This study introduces a novel eye-focused detection system designed to identify the presence of eyes within an image, offering a more efficient alternative to methods requiring full facial detection. The proposed approach utilizes a two-stage architecture: first, a coarse detector identifies potential eye regions, followed by a fine detector that confirms the presence of eyes within those areas. This method is trained on the Eye-in-the-Wild dataset and achieves a mean average precision (mAP) of 0.90, outperforming the state-of-the-art eye detection method by 0.01.

This study examines the impact of noise on mass determination for qubits and qutrits, utilizing a model where the mass is inferred from the energy spectrum of a harmonic oscillator. We analyze the performance of the Quantum Fisher Information (QFI) under two distinct error channels: the amplitude damping channel and the phase damping channel. Our findings indicate that qutrits exhibit superior noise tolerance compared to qubits, particularly when the system is subjected to amplitude damping.

This study introduces a novel method for generating highly polarized positrons with a degree exceeding 30% by utilizing a polarized electron beam and a polarized target. The approach involves directing the electron beam onto a polarized target to produce polarized positrons, which are then captured in a storage ring. Theoretical analysis indicates that the positron polarization degree is governed by the product of the electron beam's polarization and the target's polarization. Furthermore, the study demonstrates that the positron polarization degree can be enhanced by increasing the electron beam's polarization degree.

This paper examines groups with polynomial diameter, specifically addressing the question of whether such groups must have a polynomial number of conjugacy classes. We demonstrate that this is not necessarily true by constructing a family of groups with polynomial diameter that possess an exponential number of conjugacy classes. Furthermore, we establish that if a group has polynomial diameter, it must contain a nilpotent subgroup of polynomial index.

This study examines the stability of magnetic field configurations in stars, specifically focusing on the interaction between toroidal and poloidal components. We demonstrate that when these components mutually stabilize each other, the resulting field can remain stable even if the individual components are unstable on their own. Furthermore, we show that the stability of the combined field is determined by the ratio of the toroidal to poloidal magnetic energy.
This work explores the analogy between renormalization group equations and fluid dynamics, specifically examining how this relationship clarifies the nature of irreversibility in RG flows.

This paper introduces a novel search engine designed to locate both lyrics and audio for songs, addressing the limitations of standard web searches that often yield irrelevant results. The system leverages a large-scale dataset of song lyrics and audio files to train a model capable of identifying the most relevant audio tracks for any given query. Additionally, it incorporates a method to generate lyrics for songs that lack existing text. The authors evaluate the system's performance using a custom dataset of 1,000 songs, demonstrating that their approach significantly outperforms current state-of-the-art methods.

This paper introduces the notion of a topological groupoid extension, which serves as a topological stack analogue to the classical concept of a groupoid extension. We demonstrate that a topological groupoid extension is equivalent to a gerbe over a topological stack. Furthermore, we establish a correspondence between the category of topological groupoid extensions and the category of gerbes over topological stacks.

The mass growth of molecular cores is a critical factor in the formation of massive stars, yet the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. This study utilizes the ALMA Large Program on Massive Star Formation (ALMAGRAM) to investigate the mass growth of 100 massive cores within the nearby L1641 region. We find that the mass growth rate of these cores is strongly correlated with their mass, with more massive cores growing faster. This relationship is consistent with the core mass function (CMF) observed in the L1641 region, which aligns with the stellar initial mass function (SIFM) in the same area. Furthermore, the mass growth rate of these cores is comparable to the accretion rate of massive stars, suggesting that the mass growth of cores is a primary driver of massive star formation.
This paper establishes a duality between finite G\"odel algebras and finite forests, demonstrating that the category of finite G\"odel algebras is equivalent to the category of finite forests.

This study introduces a novel method for classifying 3D point cloud LiDAR data that leverages contextual information from neighboring points. The proposed approach employs a two-stage framework: first, a local context-aware feature extraction module is utilized to generate a feature vector for each point, and second, a classification module is applied to assign labels. The effectiveness of this method is demonstrated through experiments on the SemanticKITTI dataset, where it achieves a mean average precision (mAP) of 79.1%, surpassing the previous state-of-the-art result of 78.6%.

This paper investigates the impact of classical differentiation and integration on the positive definiteness of zonal functions. We establish that the derivative of a positive definite zonal function remains positive definite, whereas the integral of such a function is not necessarily positive definite. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the integral of a positive definite zonal function is positive definite if and only if the function is constant.

The recent detection of ultra-high-energy cosmic rays (UHECRs) and neutrinos by the Pierre Auger Observatory and IceCube, respectively, has sparked significant interest in their potential correlation. This study examines the implications of these findings for the correlation between UHECRs and neutrinos, utilizing a model where UHECRs are protons and neutrinos originate from the decay of neutral pions produced in proton-proton collisions. The analysis indicates that the observed correlation is consistent with a scenario where UHECRs are protons and neutrinos arise from neutral pion decay, provided the source distribution is sufficiently compact.

Liquid foams are widely utilized in industrial applications, yet their flow behavior remains poorly understood. This study introduces a novel method to characterize foam flow by analyzing the roughness factor, which quantifies the deviation of the foam's front from a straight line. The research demonstrates that this factor is governed by the foam's viscosity and the geometry of the channel, while also being influenced by the foam's drainage rate. Furthermore, the findings reveal that the roughness factor is independent of the foam's initial height.

This study introduces a novel ensemble classifier designed to enhance the performance of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) in image classification. The proposed method integrates a CNN with a Random Forest classifier, where the CNN serves as a feature extractor and the Random Forest functions as the classifier. The approach is evaluated on the CIFAR-10 dataset, demonstrating that the ensemble model outperforms the standalone CNN. Furthermore, the study analyzes the impact of varying the number of trees within the Random Forest on the overall classification accuracy.

This study examines the stability of various states within a rotating Hele-Shaw cell, specifically focusing on the impact of membrane tension. We demonstrate that the system's behavior is governed by a competition between the centrifugal force and the membrane tension. Our findings indicate that the stability of the system is determined by the ratio of the membrane tension to the centrifugal force.

This study introduces a new definition of dissipated work in thermodynamics, which is based on the internal microwork performed by a microstate. This approach is applicable to both equilibrium and non-equilibrium systems. The paper demonstrates that this definition aligns with the standard thermodynamic concept of dissipated work in equilibrium settings and also holds true for non-equilibrium systems. Furthermore, it establishes a connection between this new definition and the Jarzynski equality.

This study examines the formation of CCH and CN derivatives of cyclopentadiene (C5H5) and benzene (C6H6) in the interstellar medium, utilizing the C5H5 and C6H6 abundances derived from the Herschel Space Observatory. The findings indicate that the CCH/CN abundance ratio for cyclopentadiene is approximately 1.5 times higher than that observed for benzene. This discrepancy is attributed to the greater stability of the CCH radical within the cyclopentadiene framework compared to its benzene counterpart.

This study introduces a novel look-ahead attention mechanism for neural machine translation (NMT) that leverages the target sentence's future context to enhance the model's ability to generate the current word. By incorporating this future information, the proposed method aims to improve translation quality. Empirical evaluations on the WMT 2014 English-to-German and English-to-French translation tasks demonstrate that this approach yields significant performance gains, achieving a 0.5 BLEU point increase on the English-to-German task and a 0.3 BLEU point increase on the English-to-French task.
This paper examines the development and application of grid computing technologies through a translational approach, highlighting the significance of this methodology in advancing the field.

This study examines the evolution of a universe filled with a viscous fluid, where the viscosity coefficient is a function of the fluid's energy density. The analysis reveals that the universe's expansion history is highly sensitive to the specific form of this viscosity function. Furthermore, the model demonstrates that the universe can transition from a decelerating phase to an accelerating one, with the onset of acceleration occurring at a specific energy density determined by the viscosity function.

This study investigates how curiosity is influenced by peers, utilizing a novel dataset of 1,000 individuals who completed a curiosity assessment alongside a peer group. The findings indicate that curiosity is significantly shaped by the curiosity levels of one's peers, with this effect being stronger among those who are less curious. Furthermore, the research demonstrates that curiosity is contagious, as individuals tend to adopt the curiosity levels of their peers.

Graph Matérn Gaussian processes (GMPs) are a flexible class of non-stationary Gaussian processes that can be implemented in mini-batch and non-conjugate settings. This paper introduces a new class of GMPs that are both non-stationary and non-separable, which are constructed by combining a graph Laplacian with a Matérn kernel. We demonstrate that these models can be efficiently learned using stochastic gradient descent. Furthermore, we show that the resulting GMPs are capable of capturing complex, non-stationary patterns in data.

This study introduces a novel framework for leveraging ridesourcing vehicles to enhance sensing coverage and reliability within urban road networks. The proposed approach employs a two-stage methodology: first, it utilizes a greedy algorithm to identify the optimal set of vehicles for a specific sensing task, and second, it applies a heuristic algorithm to determine the most efficient routes for these vehicles. The effectiveness of this framework is validated through extensive simulations using real-world data from the San Francisco Bay Area, demonstrating significant improvements in both coverage and reliability compared to existing methods.

We examine the decay $J/\psi \to \text{invisible}$ as a probe for dark matter-nucleon scattering. By analyzing the $J/\psi$ decay into a pair of dark matter particles, we establish constraints on the dark matter-nucleon scattering cross section. Our findings indicate that the $J/\psi \to \text{invisible}$ decay imposes limits on the dark matter-nucleon scattering cross section that are comparable to those derived from the $J/\psi \to \text{invisible}$ decay.

This study introduces a novel class of variable stepsize SGLMs designed for nonuniform grids, which are constructed by applying a variable stepsize SGLM to a uniform grid. The resulting method is analyzed for its stability and convergence properties, with the findings indicating that the new approach is A-stable and converges at a rate of $O(h^2)$, where $h$ represents the maximum step size. Furthermore, numerical experiments are conducted to demonstrate the method's effectiveness.

This study introduces a novel method, MFSSA, which integrates the Fractional Fourier Transform (FrFT) with the Sine Cosine Algorithm (SCA) to optimize the FrFT parameter. The proposed approach is evaluated against the standard SCA and the original MFSSA algorithm using two distinct datasets: temperature curve analysis and remote sensing imagery. Results indicate that MFSSA outperforms both the standard SCA and the original MFSSA in terms of convergence speed and accuracy.

Deep-learning based automatic essay scoring (AES) models are widely used in education, yet they often exhibit oversensitivity and overstability, leading to unfair assessments. This study investigates the root causes of these issues, identifying that they stem from the models' tendency to overfit training data and their reliance on specific, non-robust features. To address this, we introduce a novel method called "Adversarial Feature Selection" (AFS), which leverages adversarial training to identify and eliminate these problematic features. Our experiments demonstrate that AFS significantly improves model robustness and fairness, resulting in a 10% reduction in the correlation between scores and features that are irrelevant to essay quality.

This study examines a random walk $S_n$ composed of independent, identically distributed increments with a zero mean and finite variance $\sigma^2$. We analyze the asymptotic behavior of the probability that the maximum of the walk exceeds a linear function of $n$, specifically $P(\max_{1 \le k \le n} S_k > bn)$, where $b$ is a positive constant. Our findings indicate that when $b$ is sufficiently large, this probability decays exponentially at a rate determined by the Cramér-Lundberg exponent. Conversely, for smaller values of $b$, the decay rate is governed by the large deviation principle associated with the random walk.

This study examines the optimization of a plasma source by analyzing the relationship between plasma parameters and the applied voltage. The investigation focuses on a specific plasma source configuration, utilizing a two-dimensional model to simulate the plasma's behavior. The simulation results indicate that the plasma's electron temperature and density are directly influenced by the applied voltage. Furthermore, the findings demonstrate that the plasma source can be optimized by adjusting the voltage to achieve the desired plasma parameters.

This study examines the dynamics of entomopathogenic nematodes (EPNs) and their target hosts, specifically focusing on the impact of EPNs on host birth rates. The model incorporates a density-dependent birth rate for the host population, which is modulated by the presence of EPNs. We demonstrate that the system can exhibit a stable equilibrium, a stable limit cycle, or a stable limit cycle with a stable equilibrium, depending on the parameter values. Furthermore, we analyze the conditions under which the system undergoes a Hopf bifurcation.

This study introduces a novel W-shaped network designed for automatic nucleus detection, which integrates a multi-scale feature extraction module with a multi-scale feature fusion module. The proposed architecture leverages a multi-scale feature extraction module to capture features at various scales, while the multi-scale feature fusion module combines these features to enhance detection accuracy. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed W-shaped network outperforms existing methods in terms of both detection accuracy and computational efficiency.

This paper establishes a local converse theorem for the rank of twists of local gamma factors, specifically for odd special orthogonal groups and symplectic groups. The proof relies on the local Langlands correspondence for these groups, which was established by Moeglin and Waldspurger.

This paper introduces the Hamiltonian path index of a graph, defined as the count of Hamiltonian paths within it. We establish a formula for the Hamiltonian path index of the Cartesian product of two graphs and apply this result to determine the index for the Cartesian product of two cycles.

The current pandemic has highlighted the critical need for effective treatments for severe cases of COVID-19. While the virus's pathogenesis is not fully understood, it is known to induce severe inflammation and tissue damage, which are primary drivers of mortality. This study investigates the potential of anti-inflammatory drugs to mitigate these effects by examining their impact on the virus's ability to trigger cell death. Specifically, we analyze how these drugs influence the virus-induced transition from apoptosis to necrosis. Our findings indicate that anti-inflammatory agents can suppress the virus's capacity to induce necrosis, thereby reducing the release of inflammatory cytokines and preventing the cytokine storm. Consequently, this suggests that anti-inflammatory drugs may serve as a viable therapeutic strategy for managing severe COVID-19 cases.

This paper introduces a novel algorithm designed to identify exogenous variables within reinforcement learning environments. By leveraging these variables, the algorithm can learn policies that are more robust to environmental changes. The proposed method is evaluated on both simulated and real-world robotic tasks, demonstrating its effectiveness in enhancing policy stability.

This paper introduces HELMHOLTZ, a tool designed to verify Michelson programs for smart contracts. HELMHOLTZ leverages the formal semantics of Michelson to generate a corresponding Coq formalization, which is then used to prove the correctness of Michelson programs. The tool is capable of verifying the correctness of Michelson programs, including those that utilize the smart contract's native storage.
